paper.title: An Efficient Pessimistic-Optimistic Algorithm for Stochastic Linear Bandits with General Constraints

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic linear bandits with general (anytime cumulative) constraints
unmapped: K_c anytime cumulative expected cost constraints E[sum_{t<=tau} W^(k)] <= 0 for every tau and k
general (nonlinear) cost functions with i.i.d. costs bounded in [-1,1]; noisy costs W^(k)(c(t),j) for all actions observed before acting
Slater's condition with constant delta_s > 0, which the learner knows and uses as input
regret measured against the optimum of a fluid LP relaxation (best context-dependent randomized policy satisfying the constraints in expectation)
i.i.d. contexts from a countable set; J actions with feature map phi(c,j) known to the learner
settings.definition_quote: The learner's objective is to learn a policy $\pi$ that maximizes the cumulative rewards over horizon $T$ subject to {\em anytime cumulative constraints}: ... $\mathbb E\left[\sum_{t=1}^{\tau} W^{(k)}\left(c(t), A^\pi(t)\right) \right] \leq 0, ~\forall\ \tau\in[T], k\in[K]$.

settings.name_in_paper: Constrained stochastic linear bandits with linear costs (costs revealed after action)
unmapped: a single anytime cumulative expected cost constraint
linear cost w(c,j) = <mu_*, psi(c,j)> in [-1,1], ||psi|| <= 1, ||mu_*|| <= 1, 1-subGaussian cost noise, cost observed only after acting (bandit feedback on the cost)
Slater's condition with constant delta_s, which the learner knows
regret against the fluid LP optimum
settings.definition_quote: After the learner takes action $A(t),$ beside receiving reward $R(c(t), A(t)),$ the learner also observes cost $$W(c(t), A(t))=w(c(t),A(t)) + \xi(t),$$ where $w(c, j) = \langle \mu_{*}, \psi(c, j) \rangle$

algorithms.name: Pessimistic-Optimistic Algorithm (LinUCB primal + queue-based dual update)

symbols.tau: round at which the regret is measured, tau <= T

conditions: Assumptions 1-3: i.i.d. contexts, r(c,j) in [0,1], ||phi|| <= 1, ||theta_*|| <= S (paper's m), 1-subGaussian noise; costs |W| <= 1 i.i.d.; Slater's condition with constant delta_s

source.label: thm:formal-UCB
source.quote: Under Assumptions 1-3, the pessimistic-optimistic algorithm achieves the following regret and constraint violations bounds for any $\tau \in [T]:$ $\mathcal R(\tau) \leq \frac{60K^{3}}{\delta^3}+ \frac{4\sqrt{6}K^{0.75}\sqrt{\tau}}{\delta} + 2 +\sqrt{8d\tau \beta_{\tau}(T^{-1}) \log \left(\frac{ d + \tau}{ d}\right)}$ ... where $\sqrt{\beta_{\tau}(T^{-1})} = m+\sqrt{2\log T + d \log \left(1+\tau/d\right)}.$

results.notes: Pseudo-regret against the fluid LP optimum. Summarised as O~((K^0.75/delta + d) sqrt(tau)). K renamed K_c because it counts constraints, not arms.
Expected constraint violation V(tau) = sum_k (E[cumulative cost])^+. It is zero for tau beyond a T-independent tau'.

symbols.kappa: positive constant independent of tau, K, delta, d

source.label: cor: tail prob
source.quote: The pessimistic-optimistic algorithm guarantees that for any $\tau \geq \frac{\kappa K^5}{\delta^2}\left(\log\left(\frac{K}{\delta}\right)\right)^2$, ... $\mathbb P\left(\sum_{t=1}^{\tau}\sum_{j\in[J]}W^{(k)}(c(t),j)X_{j}(t)>0\right)=O\left(e^{-\frac{\delta\sqrt{\tau}}{50K^{2}}}\right).$

results.notes: Bounds the probability that the sample-path cumulative cost is positive, i.e. a tail probability rather than a regret bound. The introduction states the exponent with K^{2.5}, while the corollary uses K^2.

conditions: Assumptions 1-4; single constraint (K=1); linear costs with ||mu_*|| <= 1, ||psi|| <= 1

source.label: thm:formal-UCB-W
source.quote: Under Assumptions 1-4, the pessimistic-optimistic algorithm presented in this Section achieves the following regret and constraint violations bounds for any $\tau \in [T]:$ $\mathcal R(\tau) \leq \frac{235d^4\log^4(1+T)}{\delta^3}+ \frac{(8d+24)\sqrt{\tau}\log(1+T)}{\delta}+2+10d\sqrt{\tau}\log(1+T)$

results.notes: This is the formal version of the informal Theorem 2, which states R = O~(d sqrt(tau)/delta + d^4/delta^3). The algorithm's confidence radius uses 1 in place of m, so the analysis assumes ||theta_*|| <= 1 (the paper says it used m = 1).
Expected constraint violation. It becomes zero for tau >= tau'' = O(d^2 log^2 T / delta^4), as the informal Theorem 2 states.
